facts.fact: 三十分钟后走进门庭；两只蜥蜴先后掠过砖地，第二只紧追第一只
facts.anchor: Thirty minutes later, we stepped into the courtyard. A lizard scurried across the bricks, followed by another in hot pursuit.

facts.fact: 院外是绿色棚子，前面码着一座金字塔形的柴堆；棚里三辆亮红自行车，车把旁挂着锃亮银铃
facts.anchor: Past the courtyard stood the green shed, a pyramid of firewood resting in front of it. Inside were three bright red bicycles, shiny silver bells by their handles.

facts.fact: 看着沐浴在柔光里的场景，她几乎能相信那场混乱的早晨是一场梦
facts.anchor: Gazing at the scene bathed in gentle sunlight, I could almost believe my chaotic morning had been a dream.

facts.fact: Virginia 推出车，她握住车把，磨损的皮革像黄油般柔软；Mama 很可能就是在这辆车上学会骑车
facts.anchor: the worn leather butter-soft against my fingers. Mama might well have learned to cycle on this very bike.

facts.fact: 喉咙发紧；她仍怨恨 Mama 把她孤立、把整个母系大家庭瞒住，尤其瞒住 Virginia 姨妈
facts.anchor: My throat swelled. I still resented Mama for isolating me and concealing my extended family, particularly Aunt Virginia.

facts.fact: 但在 Greer House 待了几天之后，她能想象出一个「Mama 不忍心把她暴露给 Gazzie 的冷漠」的世界
facts.anchor: I could imagine a world in which she couldn’t bear to expose me to Gazzie’s coldness.

facts.fact: 她只希望 Mama 把那段过去分享给她
facts.anchor: I just wished she’d shared that part of her past with me.

facts.fact: “Coming?” Virginia 推车经过她身边时喊
facts.anchor: “Coming?” Aunt Virginia called, walking her bike past me.

facts.fact: 两人沿与宽阔中央公路平行的人行道疾驰；几十个人往返海滩——淡彩衣配同款遮阳帽的白发女人、荧光超短裤的老先生、把红色冲浪板顶在头上的长金发男人
facts.anchor: Dozens of other people were walking or running to and from the beach—gray-haired women in pastels and matching visors, elderly men in neon short shorts, one long-haired blond man balancing a red surfboard on his head.

facts.fact: 没人说话，只在她俩骑过时点头；连蝉都安静；岛上像一座教堂，居民是端庄的会众
facts.anchor: No one spoke, though they bobbed their heads as we cycled by. Even the cicadas were quiet. The island was a church, its inhabitants a demure congregation.

facts.fact: 太阳才刚升起，湿气却无情压来；她的脑子在颅骨里胀跳；骑了十分钟她叫住 Virginia，停下后大口灌电解质水
facts.anchor: Though the sun had barely risen, humidity pressed in relentlessly. My brain throbbed against my skull. Ten minutes in, I called to Aunt Virginia.

facts.fact: “我们要掉头吗？”她不想让她在街上晕倒；天知道她怎么把人和两辆车一起拖回去
facts.anchor: “We need to turn around?” she asked. “I don’t want you passing out in the street. Lord knows how I’d drag you and both bikes back.”

facts.fact: 她差点笑呛；大多数人谈起她的病情像谈秘密——轻声、满怀担忧
facts.anchor: I nearly choked on a laugh. Most people spoke about my condition like it was a secret—quietly, and with great concern.

facts.fact: Virginia 对此有幽默感，presumably 因为她自己也是位带痛的老年女人
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia had a sense of humor about it, presumably because she was an elderly woman with her own aches and pains.

facts.fact: 她的结论：到某个阶段，你得选择哀悼自己的必死还是嘲笑它
facts.anchor: At a certain point, I think, you have to choose whether to mourn your mortality or laugh at it.

facts.fact: “只是需要缓一下”，她说，把水瓶塞进背包
facts.anchor: “Just needed a second,” I said, slipping my bottle into my backpack.

facts.fact: 路尽头是一堵沙丘墙；Virginia 把车放倒在草岗边，继续步行
facts.anchor: The road dead-ended into a wall of sand dunes. Aunt Virginia lay her bike on the side of a grassy knoll before continuing on foot.

facts.fact: 她扫视小径找顽童或任何盯上免费交通工具的人，没人多看她和车一眼
facts.anchor: I scanned the path for mischievous teens or anyone with an eye for free transportation, but no one gave me or the bikes a second look.

facts.fact: 她摇头于富人对自己财物的漫不经心，把车放在她旁边跟上去
facts.anchor: Shaking my head at the carelessness the rich displayed toward their belongings, I laid mine next to hers and followed.

facts.fact: 晨光里的 Greer House 显得歪斜，像一部老恐怖片
facts.anchor: In the morning light, Greer House had seemed off-kilter, like an old horror film.

facts.fact: Main Beach Park 尽管名字乏味，却可以是一幅画；太阳是品红的圆圈悬在暗紫地平线上，灰浪拍岸
facts.anchor: Main Beach Park, however, despite its lackluster name, could have been a painting. The sun, a magenta circle, hovered above the dusky purple horizon. Gray waves lapped the shore.

facts.fact: 她去过的海滩不多，只有 Tybee Island——离她们公寓半小时车程
facts.anchor: I hadn’t been to many beaches, only Tybee Island, which was a half-hour drive from our apartment.

facts.fact: 踩水对她的心脏太重，所以海滩日她总是坐在椅子上；Mama 躺旁边晒黑，回答她从少女杂志上读来的问题
facts.anchor: Treading water was too much for my heart, so I’d spend beach days in a chair. Mama would lie next to me, tanning as she answered questions I read from tween magazines.

facts.fact: 杂志问题的原文：若你能住在任何地方，你会住哪？城市、山里，还是海滩？
facts.anchor: If you could live anywhere, where would it be? The city, the mountains, or the beach?

facts.fact: 她打盹，脚趾轻蹭 Mama 沾沙的腿，只愿每天都这样
facts.anchor: I’d doze off, grazing her sandy legs with my toes, wishing every day were like this.

facts.fact: 和 Michelle 出事后她们就再没回过那片海滩；从前同学可能看见她、问问题
facts.anchor: We didn’t return after everything with Michelle; one of my former classmates might have seen me. Asked questions.

facts.fact: Virginia 展开橘子色毛巾啪地坐下，拍身边的空位；她把脚埋进沙，表面下一英寸出奇地凉
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia unfurled a tangerine-colored towel and plopped down, patting the empty spot beside her. I settled in, burrowing my feet into the sand. An inch below the surface, it was surprisingly cool.

facts.fact: “How do you like it?”“It’s gorgeous.”
facts.anchor: “How do you like it?” she asked.

facts.fact: 她疑惑地看她：“Really?”
facts.anchor: She looked at me quizzically. “Really?”

facts.fact: 她刮刮磨钝的脑子换个说法：“肯定比佐治亚的海滩好。”
facts.anchor: I scraped my worn mind for another way to say it. “Definitely better than Georgia beaches.”

facts.fact: “说的不是海滩，”她笑了——当天第一次笑——「是农场」
facts.anchor: “Not the beach,” she said, laughing for the first time that day. “The farm.

facts.fact: 她这周有点忙，为怠慢她感到糟糕；Mama 若知道会气疯；Mama 是出色的东道主，给客人做小行程表、端出好瓷器
facts.anchor: I’ve been a bit busy this week, and I feel awful about neglecting you. Mama would have been livid. She was a wonderful hostess. Made little itineraries for her guests. Brought out the good china.

facts.fact: 她不确定 Gazzie 有没有把擅闯的事告诉她；若没告诉她，她也不打算说
facts.anchor: I wasn’t sure if Gazzie had told her about my sneaking off, but if she hadn’t, I wasn’t about to.

facts.fact: 她不想让帮了这么多忙的 Virginia 对自己失望，答「一切顺利」
facts.anchor: I didn’t want Aunt Virginia to be disappointed in me, after all she’d done to help. “It’s going great.”

facts.fact: Virginia 反问「真的？」并说农场要适应的东西很多：血总会出现在最意想不到的地方
facts.anchor: “Really?” she asked. “The farm’s a lot to get used to. Blood ends up in the most unexpected places.

facts.fact: 她当年还帮 Gazzie 屠宰时，一次约会对象发现她肘上有血，吓了一大跳
facts.anchor: When I was still helping Gazzie with slaughtering, I had a date find some on my elbow once. Gave her a fright.

facts.fact: “没那么糟”，然后灵光一现补一句：「再没有——事情——发生了吧。」
facts.anchor: “It’s not so bad,” I said. Then, with a stroke of inspiration, I added, “No more—things—happening, though.”

facts.fact: Virginia 语气轻松地岔开：「她让你做什么？」；若她知道农场上的麻烦，也不打算告诉她
facts.anchor: “What does she have you doing?” Aunt Virginia replied lightly. If she did know anything about the trouble on the farm, she wasn’t about to tell me.

facts.fact: 「把文件数字化。跟我在萨凡纳做的差不离。」家乡的名字在唇上感觉陌生
facts.anchor: “Digitizing files. Not that far off from what I did back in Savannah.” My hometown’s name felt foreign on my lips.

facts.fact: 仿佛是一万英里远，而不是一百英里
facts.anchor: It might as well have been ten thousand miles away instead of one hundred.

facts.fact: Virginia 同情地啧舌：「我相信她领你的情。」
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia clucked her tongue sympathetically. “I’m sure she appreciates the help.”

facts.fact: 「说实话我不觉得她在乎。」她想显得不在意，听起来却仍在闹脾气
facts.anchor: “I don’t think she cares, to be honest.” I’d tried to seem unbothered but sounded petulant anyway.

facts.fact: 「她在慢慢习惯你。Harrison 待你怎么样？」
facts.anchor: “She’s getting used to you. How’s Harrison treating you?”

facts.fact: “He showed me around.”
facts.anchor: “He showed me around.”

facts.fact: 「他是个好孩子」，Virginia 若有所思地说
facts.anchor: “He’s a good boy,” Aunt Virginia said thoughtfully.

facts.fact: 她犹豫了一下还是问了——必须确定自己要面对什么：「我不知道他有时在这儿过夜。」
facts.anchor: I hesitated before asking but had to know for sure what I was up against. “I didn’t know he stayed the night sometimes.”

facts.fact: “Just in the spare room.” 叹气；但你说得对，他们很亲近
facts.anchor: “Just in the spare room.” She sighed. “But you’re right. They’re close.

facts.fact: 她说谈她继承时本该讲这件事，但不想让她恰好因此不喜欢他
facts.anchor: I should have told you when we discussed you inheriting, but I didn’t want you to dislike him, exactly.

facts.fact: 她不知如何回应；她 obviously 永远不会喜欢 Harrison
facts.anchor: I didn’t know what to say to that. I wasn’t ever going to like Harrison, obviously.

facts.fact: 几秒钟紧绷的沉默后，Virginia 又开口：你听过我们怎么认识的吗——Harrison、Gazzie 和我？
facts.anchor: After a few seconds of strained silence, Aunt Virginia spoke again. “Did you hear how we met? Harrison and Gazzie and me?”

facts.fact: “No.”
facts.anchor: “No.”

facts.fact: 她忽略了她僵硬的语气：「他用沙滩球砸了她脑袋。」
facts.anchor: She ignored my stiff tone. “He smacked her in the head with a beach ball.”

facts.fact: 她忍不住笑出声：“What?”
facts.anchor: I couldn’t help laughing. “What?”

facts.fact: Virginia  amused 地点头：一下把她打倒，然后坚持送她们两人回 Henri 家
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia nodded, amused. “Knocked her right over, then insisted on walking the two of us back to Henri’s house.

facts.fact: 「他用袭击开场、以接受一份工作邀请结束」；回来度过两个暑假，大学毕业后正式搬来
facts.anchor: He started our conversation with assault and ended it accepting a job offer. Came back for two summer breaks and moved here officially after he graduated from college.

facts.fact: 「真像 Harrison」：想迷人时迷人，真正的金童，能把任何问题变成机会的人——她永远成不了的那种人
facts.anchor: “Sounds like Harrison.” Charming when he wanted to be. A real golden boy. The kind of person who could turn any problem into an opportunity. The kind of person I’d never be.

facts.fact: 天已转蓝，水成了真正的海，不再是画家加了滤镜的样子
facts.anchor: The sky had turned blue, the water transforming into a real ocean, not some painter’s filtered vision of one.

facts.fact: Virginia 不安地捻着毛巾边，眼睛钉在推岸的浪上
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia fidgeted with the edge of the beach towel, eyes fixed on the waves as they nudged the shore.

facts.fact: 她的读法：Virginia 想让她继承，却不想把 Harrison 和她对立起来；感激涌上来，从没见过这么无私的人，真正的和事佬
facts.anchor: She wanted me to inherit but didn’t want to pit Harrison and me against each other. Appreciation washed over me. I’d never been around someone so selfless. A real peacekeeper.

facts.fact: 她主动说出口：「这是我这辈子第一个让我觉得自己正常的地方。」至少大部分时候是
facts.anchor: “This is the first place I’ve ever felt normal,” I volunteered. “Most of the time, at least.”

facts.fact: Virginia 笑：Gazzie 也一样，说她在别处都格格不入
facts.anchor: She smiled. “Gazzie’s the same way. Says she doesn’t fit in anywhere else.”

facts.fact: 短暂停顿后她抛出缅因的避暑别墅：极美，由给范德比尔特家建佛蒙特小屋的同一位建筑师设计；她每年七月都去，Gazzie 拒绝前往
facts.anchor: After a brief pause, she added, “Did you know we have a summer house in Maine? Gorgeous place. Designed by the same architect who did the Vanderbilts’ Vermont cottage. I go every July, but she refuses.

facts.fact: 「能想象吗？有那样的地方却从不去？」
facts.anchor: Can you imagine? Having a place like that and never visiting?”

facts.fact: Mama 和她去过一次 Asheville 的 Biltmore Estate——一次经典的南方朝圣；她想象不出他们一栋小屋的面积
facts.anchor: Mama and I had visited Biltmore Estate in Asheville once—a classic Southern pilgrimage. I couldn’t imagine the size of one of their cottages.

facts.fact: “Why’d she buy it, then?”
facts.anchor: “Why’d she buy it, then?”

facts.fact: 「她没买。是我们母亲盖它为了逃开。」母亲讨厌农场，十八岁时正式把农场交给 Gazzie——只在 Ida 死后一年
facts.anchor: Oh, she didn’t buy it. Our mother had it built to get away. She hated the farm, let Gazzie take over officially when she was eighteen. Only a year after Ida died.

facts.fact: 难以想象 Gazzie 不拥有 Greer House 的年代；「Gazzie 会出门吗？」
facts.anchor: It was hard to imagine a time when Gazzie didn’t own Greer House. “Does Gazzie ever leave?”

facts.fact: “Never.”
facts.anchor: “Never.”

facts.fact: 她的判断：Virginia 对 Greer House 里里外外都熟——而且暗示她知道她今早看见了什么
facts.anchor: She knew Greer House in and out—and had hinted that she knew what I’d seen that morning.

facts.fact: 她试探着说：「她早上倒不像觉得我在做梦。」
facts.anchor: “She didn’t seem to think I was dreaming earlier,” I said tentatively.

facts.fact: Virginia 揉太阳穴、深深吸气，像在给自己壮胆：「她相信她时不时会看见 Ida。」
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia rubbed her temples, then sucked in a deep breath, like she was bracing herself. “She believes she sees Ida from time to time.”

facts.fact: 她尽量慢地喝水，试图组织一个礼貌的回答
facts.anchor: I sipped from my water bottle as slowly as I could, trying to formulate a polite reply.

facts.fact: 她的既有信念：世上没有友善的鬼；按 Mama 的说法，从坟墓回来的是恶灵——Haints；而这些本就不存在
facts.anchor: There wasn’t such a thing as a friendly ghost; people who came back from the grave were, at least according to my mother, evil spirits. Haints. And those didn’t exist, anyway.

facts.fact: 她的两种自我解释：真要说，她看见的是个大活人；或者前一天吃了坏虾产生幻觉
facts.anchor: If anything, I’d seen a real person. Or eaten some bad shrimp the day before and hallucinated.

facts.fact: 这套逻辑之下压着对黑色模糊、浴水里那张脸的不安记忆
facts.anchor: Underneath that logic lay uneasy memories of the black blur, the face in my bathwater.

facts.fact: 她的推论：Gazzie 一定以为那张脸属于 Ida，这就是她急切追查的原因
facts.anchor: Gazzie must have thought the face belonged to Ida; that’s why she’d been so eager to investigate.

facts.fact: 她半信半疑地问：「你有没有……撞见过她？」
facts.anchor: “Have you ever…come across her?” I asked doubtfully.

facts.fact: Virginia 做鬼脸：「你外婆 is—was—和 Ida 很亲近」——现在时/过去时当场自我更正
facts.anchor: She grimaced. “Honey, your grandmother is—was—very close with Ida.

facts.fact: 「Ida 不是个有爱的女人。她心里有股火，像她自己是根点燃的火柴、我们全是柴火。」
facts.anchor: Ida wasn’t a loving woman. She had this anger in her, like she was a lit match and we were all firewood.

facts.fact: 她能感觉到 Ida 进屋时周身那圈怒气；她半辈子都在她靠近时躲起来
facts.anchor: You could feel when she entered Greer House, this aura of anger surrounding her. I spent half of my life hiding when I felt her coming close.

facts.fact: 她心里冒出一问：Greer House 的电流嗡鸣、那种源自某个愤怒源头的感觉——是她吗？
facts.anchor: Greer House’s electric hum, the sense that it stemmed from some furious source—was that her?

facts.fact: 她立刻自我否定：Ridiculous.
facts.anchor: Ridiculous.

facts.fact: Virginia 继续：Gazzie 怀念她，常想起共处时光——Ida 指导过她——我想她太想让 Ida 活着，所以偶尔她就——摇头——「Slips.」
facts.anchor: “But Gazzie remembers her fondly,” she continued. “She thinks about their time together often—Ida mentored her, you know—and I think she wants her to be alive so badly that occasionally she just—” She shook her head. “Slips.”

facts.fact: 松了口气，她确认：「所以你不觉得那是真的。」
facts.anchor: Relieved, I confirmed, “So you don’t think it’s real.”

facts.fact: 她犹豫后答：不，不；想象中的 Ida 在 Gazzie 压力大时出现；你妈妈走后更糟；她的整个世界翻了个面
facts.anchor: She hesitated. “No, no. Ida—imaginary Ida—shows up when Gazzie’s stressed. It got worse when your mother left. Her whole world tipped upside down.

facts.fact: 原因两层：一是想念 Caroline，二是不得不改变对这门生意的看法
facts.anchor: In part because she missed Caroline, of course, but also because she had to shift her perception of the business.

facts.fact: 她原以为会有一长串 Greer 家女性接手，但结果——再次摇头——连 Leon 都没得依靠了
facts.anchor: She’d imagined a long line of Greer women taking over, but instead—” She shook her head again. “She didn’t even have Leon to fall back on anymore.

facts.fact: Leon 从不感兴趣，但本有机会说服他；不过到那时，他已经——嗯，你知道的
facts.anchor: He wasn’t ever interested, but there’d been a chance she could convince him. Though by then, he’d— Well, you know.”

facts.fact: 浪拍岸、退去时沙子沸腾；她感觉失衡，像坐在悬崖边、脚趾悬在底下无底的黑暗上
facts.anchor: Waves crashed into the shore, sand seething as they retreated. I felt unbalanced, like I was sitting on a cliff’s edge, toes dangling into a bottomless darkness below.

facts.fact: “Leon?”“You know, Leon. Your uncle.”「我不认识什么 Leon。」她说得很慢
facts.anchor: “Leon?”

facts.fact: 她倒抽一口紧促的气：「Caroline 真的一事未告。」藏不住声音里的受伤
facts.anchor: She sucked in a tight breath. “Caroline really didn’t tell you anything,” she said, unable to hide the hurt in her voice.

facts.fact: 「他是谁？曾经是谁？」——她的问句同时问现在
facts.anchor: “Who was he? Is he?”

facts.fact: Virginia 快速眨眼，像在忍泪：「你母亲的弟弟。」
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia blinked rapidly, like she was holding back tears. “Your mother’s younger brother.”

facts.fact: 她思绪跳到 Mama 宝丽来照片里那个阴郁的男孩；又一个瞒了她多年的秘密
facts.anchor: My thoughts jumped to the sullen boy in Mama’s Polaroid pictures. Another secret, kept from me for years.

facts.fact: 翻出那封信时同样的复杂情绪：愤怒、背叛、困惑
facts.anchor: I felt the same mix of emotions I had when I’d found the letter. Anger, betrayal, confusion.

facts.fact: “Her brother?” 她的声音发抖
facts.anchor: “Her brother?” My voice trembled.

facts.fact: 「他是艺术家，和你一样。保守派。画的似乎是油画？」他厌倦了 Ida 的原作肖像，就自己动手画她
facts.anchor: “He was an artist, like you. A traditionalist. Used oils, I think? He got sick of Ida’s original portraits, so he began to paint her himself.”

facts.fact: “Can I see them?”
facts.anchor: “Can I see them?”

facts.fact: 「你已经见过了」，唇边浮起一丝笑：就挂在餐厅里
facts.anchor: “You already have,” she said, the hint of a smile on her lips. “They’re hanging in the dining room.”

facts.fact: 她试图回忆：「那场茶会？」
facts.anchor: I tried to remember them. “The tea party?”

facts.fact: 笑容扩大：「Ida 是那个长相古怪的玩偶。」
facts.anchor: Her smile grew. “Ida’s the odd-looking doll.”

facts.fact: 一声笑从她嘴里漏出：「Gazzie 知道那是她吗？」
facts.anchor: A laugh slipped out of me. “Does Gazzie know it’s her?”

facts.fact: “She hasn’t mentioned it.”
facts.anchor: “She hasn’t mentioned it.”

facts.fact: 她想见见这位舅舅：「他和 Mama 前后脚离开的吗？」
facts.anchor: I wanted to meet this uncle of mine. “Did he move away when Mama did?”

facts.fact: Virginia 站起；她急忙跟着起身，正好 Virginia 抽出身下的毛巾；视野收窄、晃了一下才站稳；那时对方已把叠好的毛巾紧抱胸前
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia stood. I scrambled to my feet in time for her to pull the towel out from under me. My vision tunneled, and I wobbled for a moment before straightening.

facts.fact: “Where did he go?” 她再次试探着问
facts.anchor: “Where did he go?” I asked tentatively.

facts.fact: 「他死于一场可怕的事故」，声音哽咽；改天我讲给你听
facts.anchor: “He died in a terrible accident,” she said, voice choked with emotion. “I’ll tell you about it sometime.”

facts.fact: 思绪飞转：又一个失去的家人、又一个谜；Virginia 伸手揉了揉她的上臂，转身离开海边
facts.anchor: My thoughts raced. Another family member, lost. Another mystery. Aunt Virginia reached out, rubbed my upper arm, and turned away from the ocean.

facts.fact: 开始慢慢走回车边；Nova 和 Gazzie 前几天都提到过事故——她们说的是 Leon 的死吗？
facts.anchor: We began our slow return to the bikes. Nova and Gazzie had both mentioned an accident the other day. Had they been referring to Leon’s death?

facts.fact: 她猜他或许与 Mama 的离开、与 Mama 被逐出家族有关
facts.anchor: Maybe he had something to do with Mama’s departure, her disowning the family.

facts.fact: 她想追问，但看到 Virginia 向下撇的嘴角，决定等
facts.anchor: I wanted to press Aunt Virginia but, seeing her downturned mouth, decided to wait.

facts.fact: 过沙丘前，她在远处海岸线上发现一个原木大小的灰绿色物体；浪撞上去它不动；她手搭凉阴指过去：「那是不是一——？」
facts.anchor: Before we passed the sand dunes, I spotted a log-sized grayish-green object along the coastline in the distance. Waves crashed against it, but it didn’t move. Shading my eyes with my hand, I pointed to it. “Is that a—?”

facts.fact: Virginia 朝同一方向看：「是。这儿不常见到，但它们能在咸水里撑一阵。大概是 exploring，或者被从沼泽冲进了海。」
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia looked in the same direction. “Yep. Don’t see them out here often, but they can handle salt water for a while. Probably exploring or got washed out to sea from the marsh.”

facts.fact: 「它会游回去吗？」——「也许。若它不游，市政府本该雇捕兽人把它挪走；不过他们可能偷懒。上一只是被打死的。」
facts.anchor: “Will it swim back?”

facts.fact: 「那怎么算偷懒？它们不危险吗？不会袭击人吗？」
facts.anchor: “Why’s that lazy? Aren’t they dangerous? Won’t they attack someone?”

facts.fact: 「那是鳄鱼（crocodiles）。它们像黄蜂——心眼坏，无缘无故也咬——但短吻鳄像蜜蜂。你不管它，它就不管你。」
facts.anchor: “That’s crocodiles, honey. They’re like wasps—mean-spirited, will bite you for the hell of it—but gators are like honeybees. They’ll let you alone, long as you let them alone, too.”

facts.fact: 她的结论：所以它们不是她一直以为的那种好杀的攻击者
facts.anchor: So they weren’t the aggressive killers I’d assumed they were.

facts.fact: 毫不在意的 Virginia 转身朝海岸回去，那头短吻鳄缓缓把头倾向太阳
facts.anchor: Nonplussed, Aunt Virginia turned back to the shore as the alligator slowly tipped its head toward the sun.

facts.fact: 还车后 Virginia 带她看 Leon 的画；细看之下她明白了：每一幅的主体都是 Ida
facts.anchor: After we returned the bikes to the shed, Aunt Virginia showed me Leon’s paintings. On closer inspection, I saw it: Each subject was Ida.

facts.fact: 她最喜欢的一幅把 Ida 画成卡通，坐在皮革面书桌前，嘴扭成夸张的怒容
facts.anchor: My favorite was of her as a cartoon at her leather-topped desk, mouth twisted into an exaggerated scowl.

facts.fact: 那幅印象派的、画她在 Greer House 下面挖掘的要暗得多：Leon 把她画成披斗篷的身影， horns 的隐约轮廓从发髻里伸出
facts.anchor: The impressionist painting of her digging under Greer House was much darker. Leon had rendered her as a cloaked figure, the faint outline of horns sticking out of her updo.

facts.fact: 「真不敢相信 Gazzie 没看出来」——考虑到她热衷名画修复
facts.anchor: “I can’t believe Gazzie hasn’t noticed,” I said. “Given she’s into painting restoration.”

facts.fact: “Ah”——Virginia 的眼神从她这里滑开——「那个啊。」
facts.anchor: “Ah,” Aunt Virginia said, her eyes sliding away from mine. “That.”

facts.fact: 她打量 Virginia，困惑：是不舒服，还是不感兴趣？
facts.anchor: I studied her, confused. Was she uncomfortable, or just disinterested?

facts.fact: 「她只修复原作，Ida 亲自委托的那些」：Gazzie 书房里的收藏、客厅的肖像、农场上办公室那幅画；她对别的艺术没眼光
facts.anchor: “She only works on the originals, the ones Ida herself commissioned,” she continued. “The collection in Gazzie’s study, the portrait in the parlor, and the painting in the farm’s front office. She doesn’t have eyes for other art.”

facts.fact: 当天晚些时候 Virginia 出门办事，她去 Gazzie 办公室想问舅舅的事，庆幸走廊上没有陌生人
facts.anchor: When Aunt Virginia disappeared on one of her errands later that morning, I made my way to Gazzie’s office to ask about my uncle, relieved to find the hallway stranger-free.

facts.fact: 敲门无人应；她把门开一条缝怕对方没听见，屋里却空着；Ida 的肖像们盯着她，直到她关上门
facts.anchor: She didn’t respond to my knock. I cracked open the office door in case she hadn’t heard, but the room was empty. Ida’s portraits stared me down until I closed the door.
